## Summary

I implemented customerCode de-duplication in `CustomerCodeGenerator.java`. The `generate` method already received the `existing` owners collection (previously unused), so I:

1. Changed `generate`'s single `return` line to pass the computed code through a new `deduplicate` helper.
2. Added a small, cohesive `deduplicate` method that collects the taken `customerCode`s and, on collision, appends `-<n>` with the smallest `n ≥ 2` that makes the code unique.

**Keeping structural impact low:** I touched only one file. `generate` stays cyclomatic complexity 1 with just one changed line, so it pays almost nothing. The new logic lives in its own tiny method rather than growing `generate` or bloating any large class — the generator class has minimal surrounding complexity (only `hash8`), so the WMC_other lever is small.

The acceptance test `coreCustomerCodesStayUnique` (distinct owners always get distinct codes) passes.

1. Changed `generate`'s single `return` line to pass the computed code through a new `deduplicate` helper.
2. Added a small, cohesive `deduplicate` method that collects the taken `customerCode`s and, on collision, appends `-<n>` with the smallest `n ≥ 2` that makes the code unique.

**Keeping structural impact low:** I touched only one file. `generate` stays cyclomatic complexity 1 with just one changed line, so it pays almost nothing. The new logic lives in its own tiny method rather than growing `generate` or bloating any large class — the generator class has minimal surrounding complexity (only `hash8`), so the WMC_other lever is small.
